## Blood Pressure Trend Visualization for Lifestyle Tracking

For a 58-year-old without emergency symptoms, the clearest way to show this log is a **time-series line chart** with two lines for **morning systolic** and **evening systolic**. If you want a fuller view, add lighter secondary lines or markers for the diastolic readings.

## Best Chart Setup and What It Shows

**Recommended chart type**
- **Primary choice:** Line chart
- **Best layout:** One chart with 4 lines, or 2 stacked panels:
  - Top: systolic morning vs evening
  - Bottom: diastolic morning vs evening
- **Why this works:** It makes the downward pattern from lifestyle changes easy to see, and it shows the consistent gap between morning and evening readings.

**Axis labels**
- **X-axis:** Date
- **Y-axis:** Blood pressure (mmHg)
- **Legend labels:** Morning systolic, Morning diastolic, Evening systolic, Evening diastolic

**Helpful chart details**
- Use a horizontal reference band or line around **130/80 mmHg** to show a common comparison point.
- Keep the same scale across the whole chart so changes are easy to compare.
- Use markers on each reading to make the step-by-step improvement visible.

## What the Graph Suggests

| Observation | What a clinician or patient could notice |
|---|---|
| Steady downward trend | Both morning and evening pressures fall across the 11-day period, which is consistent with improvement over time. |
| Morning readings stay higher | Morning systolic and diastolic values are consistently above evening values, suggesting a predictable daily pattern. |
| Systolic improves more visibly | Morning systolic drops from 148 to 135 and evening systolic from 142 to 132, showing a clear reduction. |
| Diastolic also trends down | Morning diastolic falls from 92 to 85 and evening diastolic from 88 to 82, indicating improvement on both measures. |

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Plot as line chart] https://www.google.com/search?q=line+chart+blood+pressure+time+series
Action: [Button: Compare to BP ranges] https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings

## Sources

- American Heart Association blood pressure basics: https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings
- NHS blood pressure overview: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/high-blood-pressure-hypertension/
- CDC high blood pressure information: https://www.cdc.gov/bloodpressure/
